name: Advanced Mathematical Models
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student - gains knowledge in a chosen advanced mathematical modeling and/or data analysis method, - is able to apply the method in practical data, - is able to make conclusions from the results and present them in written form.
content: The completion of the course will provide the student with chosen area advanced skills needed to conduct large-scale mathematical modelling exercises or create large computational data sets. The course will not be directly part of doctoral thesis work and it can be passed twice if the topic of modelling is different.

name: Advanced Simulation Methods in Applied Mathematics
learningOutcomes: A course to practice simulation skills in realistic system simulations in an engineering, scientific or financial modelling context.
content: The exact contents will be discussed between the graduate student and her/his supervisor on a case-by-case basis but they are expected to involve substantial software development work in simulation methods. The completion of the course will provide the student with skills needed to conduct large-scale simulations. The course will not be directly part of doctoral thesis work and it can be passed twice if the topic of modelling is different.

name: Applied Mathematics I
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student knows the numerical methods for solving linear and nonlinear equations and estimating derivatives and integrals. The student can apply these skills to solve engineering problems involving differential equations and optimization problems numerically. The student can document their problem-solving process. The student may familiarize themselves in the use of AI in assisting technical problem-solving, programming and technical writing.
content: Rehearsal of calculus and other basics as necessary. Numerical differentiation and integration, numerical solutions of linear and nonlinear equations and systems of equations, differential equations, and numerical optimization with applications in design and engineering problems. Company cooperation It is possible to do the course project with a company. Use of AI applications Use of AI applications to assist problem-solving, programming and improving the student's own writing
prerequisites: Recommended: Basics of calculus and programming, introduction to Matlab.
equivalentCoursesInfo: This course may replace BK20A1501 Numeeriset menetelmät I for LES students.

name: Applied Mathematics II
learningOutcomes: After having completed the course, the student can apply the theory on statistics including concepts of probability and randomness on interpreting technical and scientific data. Student can apply the normal distribution and other common distributions on interpreting variance. Student can fit a model to statistical data and estimate the model error. Student understands the principles of planning empirical experiments and can design experiments based on theoretical models. Student can apply the methods for reducing the required amount of samples and can compute the error estimates for such experiments allowing to reduce cost of experiments.
content: The more detailed teaching content of the course can be divided under the three main themes: A) Statistical and probabilistic concepts and combinatorics, B) probability distribution functions, and C) testing statistical data and evaluating goodness of fits to statistical data. Below is the contents contained within each main theme. Of these, the core of the course is the basic knowledge of these topics. Any content on the course, which is not the core of the course, is always reported separately. A) Population and sample, permutations, combinations, and probabilities. B) Probability distribution functions and cumulative distribution functions, normal distribution, student distribution, and chi-distribution. C) Testing for mean or variance, confidence intervals and testing the goodness of fit for statistical data.
prerequisites: Recommended: basic knowledge of statistics and spreadsheet calculations.
equivalentCoursesInfo: This course may replace BM20A1401 Tilastomatematiikka I for LES students.

name: Discrete Mathematics
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student is expected to know and understand the basic concepts of discrete mathematics, be able to formulate models representing simple discrete problems and solve them.
content: Main concepts in mathematical reasoning, relations, combinatorics and graph theory.
prerequisites: Some basic mathematics & statistics course.

name: Engineering Mathematics 1
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student knows the theory of mathematical functions, derivation integration, vectors, vector computations, matrices, coordinate transforms, parametric curves, polar coordinates and curves, and complex numbers. In addition to analytical methods, student can perform numerical derivation and integration on single variate functions. The student can solve simple mathematical problems related to previously mentioned topics in electric, energy, environmental and mechanical engineering.
content: Rehearsal and advancement of the students' knowledge of functions, calculus and vectors. Introduction to matrix computations and handling various coordinate systems, as well as to parametrical curves and complex numbers. Applications of the theory in electric, energy, environmental and mechanical engineering.

name: Engineering Mathematics 2
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student knows the basic theory on partial derivative and gradients, multiple integration, mathematical series such as Taylor series, vector fields and vector operators. The student can solve simple differential equations and systems of differential equations. The student can solve simple mathematical problems related to mentioned topics in electric, energy, environmental and mechanical engineering. The student knows the basic theory on integral transforms, methods of optimization, statistical description of data, probability, randomness, normal distribution and other common distributions. Student knows how to fit a model to statistical data and estimate the model error. The student knows how to apply integral transforms, numerical optimization, or statistics on simple engineering problems.
content: Introduction to partial differentiation, differential equations and numerical computation, as well as to more advanced topics of integral transforms such as Laplace and Fourier transforms, numerical analysis, optimization, statistics and probability. Advanced integral and vector calculus, and applications of the theory in science and technology.
prerequisites: LES10A010 Engineering Mathematics 1

name: Engineering Mathematics I
learningOutcomes: After completing this course, students will learn calculations and the utilization of formulas and identities to simplify mathematical expressions and solve equations. Moreover, they will grasp the concepts of limits and derivatives, enabling them to evaluate questions related to these topics by applying the rules of limits and derivatives, and understanding their applications in engineering problems. Additionally, students will acquire the ability to evaluate various types of integrals and measure the area and volume of geometrically shaped bodies, and applications in Engineering (electrical, energy & environmental, and mechanical). Furthermore, they will develop a basic understanding of modeling and solving initial value problems.
content: Function theory: definition of difference types of functions, inverse function, composite function, and their inverse, usage of functions in engineering problems Trigonometric functions: Definitions, identities of trigonometric functions, modelling waves, current waveforms, sinusoidal voltage signals. Limit: definition of limit, continuity and discontinuity, limit of composite functions. Differentiation: slope, Newton Quotient, definition of limit, rules of differentiation, Chain rule, higher order derivative, rate of change, monotonicity, maximum and minimum, extrema, application problems in engineering, L'Hôpital's rule. Integration: definition and rules of integration, initial values problems, change of variables, Riemann sums and definite integral, applications of integration (mean and average of a function, area under the curve, area bounded by region, arc length, volume of solid), techniques of integration.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of fundamental mathematics

Furthermore, they will develop a basic understanding of modeling and solving initial value problems.

Differentiation: slope, Newton Quotient, definition of limit, rules of differentiation, Chain rule, higher order derivative, rate of change, monotonicity, maximum and minimum, extrema, application problems in engineering, L'Hôpital's rule. Integration: definition and rules of integration, initial values problems, change of variables, Riemann sums and definite integral, applications of integration (mean and average of a function, area under the curve, area bounded by region, arc length, volume of solid), techniques of integration.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of fundamental mathematics

name: Engineering Mathematics II
learningOutcomes: After completing this course, students will achieve the knowledge of parametrizing curves and solving related problems. Moreover, they will gain conceptual understanding of matrices and their operations, along with applications. Students will be able to interpret engineering problems using vectors and find solutions by applying vector properties and operations. They will also attain knowledge of complex numbers, their mappings, and applications of analytic and harmonic functions in engineering (electrical, energy & environmental, and mechanical).
content: Curves: Curves and their types, parametric equations, length of curve, area of surface of revolution. Coordinates: Polar coordinates, cylindrical and spherical coordinates, and their applications Matrices : Definition and operations on matrices, pixel, applications to transformation, determinant, Cramer’s rule, inverse of matrix, solving system of linear equations, Gaussian elimination, eigenvalues, characteristic equation. Vectors: Definition, dot product, cross product, work, are of parallelogram, volume of parallelepiped, coplanar vectors, vector equation of line, distance from a point to line or plane, applications in engineering. Complex analysis : Definition, operations of complex numbers, polar form, Euler’s formula, complex mappings, functions of complex variables, analytic function, harmonic function, applications in engineering, Möbius transformation, conformal mappings, and their applications in engineering.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of fundamental mathematics

name: Engineering Mathematics III
learningOutcomes: After completing this course, students will learn simple modeling and solving of first-order and simple higher-order linear differential equations, along with their applications in engineering. Moreover, students will achieve knowledge in dealing with vector-valued functions, motion, curvature, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, double and triple integrals, and their applications. Furthermore, students will grasp the concept of vector fields and operators (gradient, curl, divergent), line integrals, potential energy, and their applications in engineering.
content: Differential equations: Introduction to differential equations DE, separable DE, Exact DE, Homogeneous DE, first-order DE, Bernoulli DE, Simple higher-order DE, applications of DEs in engineering. Vector-valued functions: Derivative and integration of vector functions, motion, angular velocity, unit tangent and normal, curvature. Double & triple integration: Functions of several variables, limit, partial derivative, double and triple integration, and their applications in engineering. Vector fields: Gradient, curl, divergent, line integral, independence of path, potential energy, applications in engineering.
prerequisites: LES10A210 or corresponding knowledge

name: Engineering Mathematics IV
learningOutcomes: After completion of this course, students will be able to achieve knowledge of handling probability, Bernoulli, binomial, and normal distribution. Moreover, students will learn how to find the solution of a differential equation applying Laplace transformation. In addition, students will be able to transfer the given functions in terms of Fourier series and will learn its applications in engineering (electrical, energy & environmental, and mechanical).
content: Statistics: Mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, sampling. Probability: Counting methods, laws of probability, conditional probability and independence, random variables, measurement error, Bernoulli distribution, Binomial distribution, normal distribution, application problems. Laplace Transforms: Introduction, Laplace transform of derivative and integration, inverse Laplace transforms, solving differential equations by Laplace transform, applications in engineering. Fourier Transforms: Introduction, expressing in terms of Fourier series, integral properties of even and odd functions, orthogonality relations, Fourier series of even and odd functions, Parseval’s theorem, applications in engineering. Numerical derivative and integration.
prerequisites: LES10A220 Engineering Mathematics III or LES10A210 Engineering Mathematics III

name: Engineering Mathematics IV (HDD)
learningOutcomes: After completion of this course, students will be able to achieve knowledge of handling probability, Bernoulli, binomial, and normal distribution. Moreover, students will learn how to find the solution of a differential equation applying Laplace transformation. Laplace Transforms: Introduction, Laplace transform of derivative and integration, inverse Laplace transforms, solving differential equations by Laplace transform, applications in engineering. Fourier Transforms: Introduction, expressing in terms of Fourier series, integral properties of even and odd functions, orthogonality relations, Fourier series of even and odd functions, Parseval’s theorem, applications in engineering. Numerical derivative and integration.

name: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning
learningOutcomes: The student is able to 1) understand the key mathematical principles for machine learning (ML), 2) utilise mathematical theory to show relevant characteristics of selected ML approaches, 3) experimentally study the advantages and limitations of the approaches and 4) deepen the understanding in a selected case study.
content: Mathematical bases for machine learning: principles of learning, linear algebra and geometry, norms and proximity measures, information theory, loss functions, parameter estimation, differentiation and optimisation, probability, statistics and Bayesian inference, curse of dimensionality and decomposition, model selection and evaluation. Company cooperation: no direct cooperation. Use of AI applications: readily available AI tools can be used for checking the language of written reports.
prerequisites: Ability to program in Matlab or Python.

name: Mathematics A
learningOutcomes: This course discusses and explains the fundamental topics of software engineering-related areas of mathematics. At the end of the course the student will be able to: 1. Understands the fundamental concepts of set theory, functions, logic and matrices. 2. Is capable of performing simple mathematical calculations and solve simple equations independently by applying the taught topics in appropriate context. 3. Understand and identify issues related to the applied concepts taught in this course.
content: The Basics of Discrete Mathematics: set theory, functions, logic and proofs, number theory and matrices. How to talk about mathematical objects precisely.

name: Mathematics for Economics
learningOutcomes: After taking the course, the students should be able to: - Estimate elemental probabilities - Solve basic equations (polynomial, exponential, logarithmic) - Analyze the behavior of elemental functions using equations and differential & integral calculus - Perform basic matrix calculations and solve systems of linear equations using matrices - Model and analyze cost, revenue and profit with functions - Understand arithmetic and geometric series & their connection with loan and investment calculations as well as perform these calculations using different interest rates.
content: Probability theory, equation solving, functions and function behavior analysis, differentiation, integration. Linear algebra, matrix calculations, Gaussian elimination. Functions in business (cost, revenue, profit), financial applications of differential and integral calculus. Arithmetic and geometric series, loan and investing calculations.

name: Mathematics in Technology 1
learningOutcomes: Student is able to: - regognise different polynomial equations and polynomial graph - solve inequalities - solve simultaneous equations with the software - solve basic space vectors - utilise space vectors - solve exponential and logarithm functions
prerequisites: Details available in Completion methods under the header Teaching

name: Mathematics in Technology 2
learningOutcomes: Student is able to - solve challenging functions - solve basic derivation functions and utilise derivation in practice - solve integrated polynomial functions and utilise integration in practice - solve trigonometrical problems
prerequisites: Details available in Completion methods under the header Teaching

name: Mathworks Self-Study Courses
learningOutcomes: The course deepens students' understanding of the specialized topics in matlab through a set of online courses. There are two possible modules for student to do one credit each. In addition if one wants to do three credits one additional module can be agreed with responsible teacher. Module ‘Data processing and visualization' By the end of the module student will be able to import tabular data. Preprocess data. Handle graphics formatting Functions. Import data from multiple files. Analyze group within data. Import unstructured data. Module ‘Matlab programming techniques' By the end of the module student will be able to use development tools in Matlab to assist in understanding, debugging and optimizing code. Creating a test framework to determine if the application is behaving as expected. Writing functions that can handle flexible user input values and display relevant error messages when appropriate. Reviewing of selection of Matlab data types. Organizing data in Matlab through the use of various data types. Modifying the structure of code files. Writing better and more efficient code. Sharing applications using toolboxes.
content: Module ‘Data processing and visualization' Module consists of importing column oriented data files that contain a mixture of data types. Handling missing value and categorical data. Creating sophisticated visualizations using matlab graphics objects. Reading large data stored in multiple files. Identifying groups within data and analyzing them. Plotting irregularly spaced data. Importing blocks of data into matlab. Module ‘Matlab programming techniques' Utilize development tools. Verifying Application Behavior. Creating robust applications. Review of data types. Structuring data. Structuring code. Performance and memory. Creating a toolbox. Possible third module to be discussed with the responsible teacher in case of wanting to do three credit course.

name: Must-Have Math for Decision Makers
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, students will be able to: perform basic operations over mathematical objects and operators: matrix, polynomial, derivative, integral, equation/inequation, differential equations, mean/variance, regression, etc. know basic optimization strategies code/operate the above mentioned in MATLAB and/or Python
content: Basics of linear algebra, probability theory, differential equations and optimization, programming in MATLAB-Simulink and Python

name: Project Work in Engineering Mathematics 2
learningOutcomes: The student advances their knowledge of mathematical theory or gains practical knowledge from applying mathematical skills in analyzing, modelling or optimizing a problem related to their field of studies. The course prepares the student for advanced studies leading up to the writing of an M.Sc. thesis or doctoral studies and scientific research. The student gains insight into the role of digitalization and mathematical models, including AI tools, in the future life, society and business.
content: A specific project is done as either a theoretical study, laboratory experiments or in a suitable commercial co-operator. The project is planned with the supervisor and may consist of laboratory work, literature research and/or theoretical studies, reporting, article writing or problem-solving in industry. The course underlines the importance of understanding the computer models of the student’s field that are driving much of industry and business and the role of digitalization in changing business models. Company cooperation The project work may be done for a company. Use of AI applications AI applications are an example of the "computer models" and may optionally be used or studied in the project.

name: Seminar on Mathematical Sciences
content: Scientific seminar, if you need this course for your studies, please contact the lecturer

name: Statistical mathematics
learningOutcomes: At the end of the course the student will be able to: 1. Understands the concepts of variables, probabilities, uncertainty, and distributions. 2. Can define a statistical problem based on the given dataset and solve them with the methods given at the course. 3. Is capable of performing simple statistical analysis tasks with appropriate statistical tools.
content: Probability calculus. Random variables and basic probability distributions. Data and descriptive statistics. Basics of statistical inference. Parameter estimation. Hypothesis testing. Correlation and simple regression analysis. Application of statistical software. Introduction to R-programming language.

name: Basics of Engineering Mathematics
learningOutcomes: The goal of the course is to repeat, deepen and expand the high school knowledge about functions, differential calculus and vectors, as well as to introduce concepts of matrix algebra in particular, solving linear systems of equations, and also the basics of MATLAB. After the course the student knows basic concepts on aforementioned topics and know how to apply these in simple problems.
content: The basics of functions, derivative, integral, vectors, matrices and MATLAB.
equivalentCoursesInfo: BM20A7850 Basics of Engineering Mathematics replaces BM20A7800 Basics of University Mathematics for Chemical Engineering, Software Engineering and Industrial Engineering and Management students.

name: Mathematical Modelling
learningOutcomes: Student understands the applicability of mathematical models to solving different real-life problems, and is able to formulate models and assess their suitability, and acquire knowledge and skills for studying more demanding applications. Student understands the modeling process, knows types of models and conservation principles. He/she is able to formulate models using differential equations, discrete, probabilistic and fuzzy concepts. The student knows how to use data and perform parameter estimation and understands the ideas of approximation and scales.
content: Mathematical applications, stages of the modelling process. Different types of models. Conservation principles and basics of models. Differential equations and systems theory. Discrete models. Models, data and parameter estimation. Equilibrium models and stability. Approximation and scales. Probabilistic models. Case examples.
prerequisites: Recommended: BM20A1401 Statistics I BM20A1601 Matrix Calculus, BM20A6700 Mathematics I, BM20A6800 Mathematics II, BM20A6900 Mathematics III, fysiikan 1. vuoden opinnot.

name: Extension Course on Mathematical Analysis
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to give deeper understanding of content of first year courses on calculus, linear algebra and differential equations. After course the student has a deeper understanding on the theory behind methods presented on these courses, knows extensions for these methods and has wider knowledge of applications.
content: Topics will include for example: different projections, uniform continuity and convergence, approximations with polynomials, measures for error, series expansion of functions of several variables, history of mathematics, methods of solving differential equations, Lagrange method with inequality constraints, basics of compression of signals. Seminar lectures about mathematics in solving engineering problems. Content of the course will have slight variation on different years.
prerequisites: Recommended BM20A6700 Mathematics I, BM20A6800 Mathematics II.
equivalentCoursesInfo: Opintojakso poistuu lv 21-22 jälkeen ja korvataan tutkinnossa tapauskohtaisesti.

name: Mathematics and Physics Tutoring

content: Student on this course will participate as tutor to exercises on physics or mathematics courses and to meetings, in which matters concerning tutoring are discussed.
prerequisites: At most 15 applicants are selected for the course based on suitability. Prerequisite: a good grades in first year mathematics or physics studies.

name: Mathematics III
learningOutcomes: After the course, the student knows the principles of the study of the behavior of function of several variables. In simple cases, student is able to form models and solve problems using functions of several variables. In addition, the student knows the basics of using series.
content: Limits and extreme values (also constrained) for functions of several variables. The chain rule, gradient and directional derivative. Differentiation for implicite functions and the existence inverse mapping. The least squares method. Convergence of series. Power series, Taylor polynomials and series (also an error estimate). Introduction Fourier cosine and sine series.

learningOutcomes: Hyväksytyn kurssisuorituksen jälkeen, opiskelija ymmärtää systemaattisen matemaattisten haasteiden osiin pilkkomisen ja ratkaisemisen perusteet LUT:lla opetettujen käytänteiden tyyppisillä tavoilla.
